paths.description: Entry page and primary content-discovery template; tested default, dark, contrast, reduced-motion, mobile, no-JS, security, network, accessibility, performance, and memory conditions.
Representative video listing/index template; selected to cover long grids, filters, navigation, and mobile reflow.
Representative media detail/playback template; selected for media layout, content metadata, and visual stability.
Primary account form; selected for labels, validation, autocomplete, auth, and mobile reflow.
Unknown route; selected to judge HTTP/network failure recovery.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Screenshot under dark preference and computed styles show color-scheme: normal and the same light rgb(236,236,236) body surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “dark-mode” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-contrast / forced-colors: controls, text and scrollbars remain visible under high-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: Axe found 118 serious color-contrast failures; the high-contrast capture provides visual corroboration.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “dark-mode” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no authored view-transition CSS, and route changes are full abrupt document navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: The long listing pages use static navigation chrome; CSS/DOM inspection found no scroll-state or progress treatment to orient users.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: Tooltips, popovers and menus use CSS anchor positioning (with fallback positions) so they stay attached and reposition correctly rather than being manually positioned.
findings.evidence: Language and login overlays are Bootstrap-style div modals; the probe found zero popover/dialog elements and no anchor-positioning implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: Route and modal navigation provides no directional transition, highlight, or authored view-transition cue for the moved context.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM/CSS contains fixed, z-index 9999 third-party video-ad slider chrome and the screenshots show advertising competing with the content.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: The page uses custom div-based .modal overlays and manual Bootstrap dismissal; zero dialog, popover, or details elements were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: First-viewport screenshots show dense toolbars, filters, ad placements, and borders competing with the video content.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: Layout adapts to narrow viewports with no horizontal overflow and no fixed pixel widths forcing a desktop layout on mobile; viewport meta present; fluid scaling and intrinsic sizing rather than brittle breakpoints.
findings.evidence: At 360px, home, videos, and video-detail overflow by 540-555px (scroll widths 900-915px).
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css-layout” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero container-query rules; reused listing components retain a desktop-width layout and cause mobile overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css-layout” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: The focused navigation link computed to outline none 0px, and the target probe found multiple visible controls only 19px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “css-layout” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Loading, empty, success, error, offline, and partial-completion states are visible and actionable; users can retry, undo, cancel, go back, or continue without losing context.
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty signup exposed no validation messages, invalid controls, alerts, or recovery guidance; an unknown route falls through to Chrome’s bare HTTP 404 page.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “forms” and verify with the same signup evidence condition.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.1s and CLS 0.107, outside good thresholds, despite TBT 0ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “performance” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: The mobile video detail layout observer measured CLS 0.172 with a dominant late shift of 0.143.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “performance” and verify with the same video-detail evidence condition.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR shows six parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets plus a synchronous parser-inserted jQuery 1.11.1 script in the critical path.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “performance” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “performance” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.evidence: The video/content homepage exposes zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph metadata despite representing rich media entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “security” and verify with the same global evidence condition.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: The load contacts 14 third-party origins including known Google trackers and opaque ad/tracking domains; third parties account for 868,870 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “security” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “security” and verify with the same signup evidence condition.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “security” and verify with the same global evidence condition.

findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same browse evidence condition.

findings.summary: Where the site is an app, it is installable (web app manifest) and offers an offline fallback and works on flaky networks. (Contextual: a brochure or intrinsically-online site may reasonably not need this.)
findings.evidence: The media application provides no web app manifest or installable metadata; no offline fallback was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: HTTP errors, network failures, timeouts and stale data states are handled intentionally: users see useful recovery options rather than blank screens, infinite spinners, broken shells, or misleading success states.
findings.evidence: A missing route displays Chrome’s generic HTTP ERROR 404 page with no branded explanation, navigation, search, or recovery links.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same error evidence condition.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: The page declares lang=en while prominently rendering Japanese titles and offers RTL languages through # links without a page direction strategy.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “html” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: No deceptive design: no confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised ads, or nagging consent walls; honest defaults; clear pricing and consent; easy reversal/cancel; predictable, declaratively-wired actions; and no hidden-text tricks (hidden content stays deep-linkable and indexable rather than used to deceive).
findings.evidence: Opaque third-party advertising scripts and fixed high-z-index ad chrome compete with content without an evident consent or preference surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “forms” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Forms prevent and recover from mistakes humanely: validate after interaction (not prematurely), give clear required-field feedback, announce errors accessibly, and signal invalid fields visibly rather than blaming the user.
findings.evidence: Empty signup submission produced no browser validation message, :invalid fields, alert role, or visible error state.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “forms” and verify with the same signup evidence condition.

findings.summary: Input is assisted, not obstructed: correct autocomplete tokens so address, payment, sign-in and sign-up fields autofill, and inputs are highlighted/sized to help the user rather than trip them up.
findings.evidence: Signup username, password, confirmation, and email fields all have empty autocomplete values; login fields do too.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “forms” and verify with the same signup evidence condition.

findings.summary: Checkout, subscription, consent, authentication and account-management flows are clear, reversible, and proportionate: pricing and commitments are visible, cancellation is findable, sensitive actions re-authenticate when appropriate, and users are not tricked into continuity.
findings.evidence: Account creation and login are password-only, omit autocomplete/passkey support, and expose no modern reauthentication affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “forms” and verify with the same signup evidence condition.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: All 25 audited images lack srcset and modern formats; 20 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “optimize-image-priority” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: The initial page performs 58 requests, 56 third-party, with duplicate ad-provider scripts and analytics before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “optimize-image-priority” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third-party resources consume 868,870 of 886,697 transferred bytes; scripts are 409KB and fonts 212KB on the entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “optimize-image-priority” and verify with the same home evidence condition.

findings.summary: Repeating a representative interaction (open/close a modal, navigate a route and back, infinite-scroll a list) about 10 times does not grow retained heap without bound; what is allocated during the interaction is released when it ends.
findings.evidence: After ten login-modal open/close cycles, the heap summary rose from 9,023,564 to 10,511,868 bytes and from 167,313 to 187,182 nodes; this is a leak signal requiring retained-path confirmation.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow Modern Web Guidance “performance” and verify with the same home evidence condition.
